reflection.text:
Unblinded truth: Aurora kinase inhibitors — verdict APPROVE, agent correct at p=0.85. This was a clean phenotypic call, not a literature-anchored call, and the reflection needs to be explicit about why.

What the evidence got right:

Acquisition captured the saturated polyploidy signature early and then replicated it across independent doses. e2 (0.3 uM): frac_large_nucleus z=+31.1, nuc_area +19.0, cell_area +17.1; e3 (10 uM): frac_large_nucleus +28.9, cell_area +26.5, nuc_area +20.0. e6 (0.03 uM - the lowest dose we sampled): cell_area +32.6, frac_large_nucleus +32.1, nuc_area +19.8. e7 (1 uM): frac_large_nucleus +24.2, cell_area +19.5, nuc_area +17.2. Four independent wells, four doses spanning 0.03 to 10 uM (of the 8-dose 0.01-30 uM plate in e1), all with z ~ +17 to +32 for nuclear and cell area. That magnitude and replication is what made p=0.84/0.85 calibrated despite single-replicate-per-dose.

Comparison to atlas was discriminative, not just supportive. e4 over 2 wells: NSC 1/2 Aurora, k-neighbours 6/10 Aurora vs 2/10 DNA damage, 2/10 DNA replication. e8 over 4 wells: NSC 3/4 Aurora, k-neighbours still 6/10 Aurora vs 2/10 each for the other two. The only non-Aurora NSC vote was the 10 uM well, consistent with high-dose off-target toward DNA damage/replication neighbors but not flipping the majority. DNA damage/replication were correctly kept at 0.08 and 0.05 in e13, microtubule stabilizers/destabilizers, actin disruptors and Eg5 at 0.01-0.005, because e5 microscopist on 4 fields explicitly reported lower density vs DMSO with intact tubulin/actin and 7 observations favoring Aurora, with frac_mitotic_like absent. That visual exclusion is why Eg5/microtubule calls were not inflated by the large-cell phenotype.

What misled or was flagged incorrectly:

We listed e9 (frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2) and e11 (nuc_dna_integrated rho=-0.80 p=0.2) as contradicting in e13, along with e12 rho=-0.80 and e10 rho=+0.20 p=0.8 for nuc_area. In hindsight this was misinterpretation of dose_response with n=4. When the effect is already maximal at the lowest sampled dose (e6 z=+32.1 at 0.03 uM), Spearman cannot be positive; the slight decline from +32 to +24-28 across doses creates a negative rho that is flat/saturated, not dose-independent. All p-values were 0.2-0.8, i.e. no power, so they should not have been weighted as contradiction. The review critique is correct: saturation, not lack of dose dependence.

Acquisition choices and their limits:

We sampled mid-low then high (e2->e3) to test onset vs maximal, then filled in low (e6) and intermediate (e7) and then relied on atlas vote + visual. That was efficient but left gaps: we never acquired 0.01 uM or 30 uM, so we have no true no-effect level and no toxicity ceiling; we inferred potency from "already maximal at 0.03 uM" rather than from an EC50 curve. Single-replicate-per-dose was mitigated only by the same massive effect replicating across 4 doses and by e5 visual replication across 4 fields, not by within-dose replication.

Compound and literature context:

After submit, e15 lookup confirmed AZ-A is an internal BBBC021 code with CID none, ChEMBL none, no curated mechanism and no structure to validate chemically — so orthogonal chemical validation was impossible. We had to rely on phenotype alone, flagged correctly in the conclusion's next-experiment suggestion (flow DNA 4N/8N + phospho-H3 Ser10/Aurora B assay vs gamma-H2AX) rather than chemistry.

Literature found in this run did not support the imaging phenotype directly. e16 and e18 returned 0 hits for 'polyploidy large nuclei' and HCS polyploidy queries. e17 and e19 returned generic Aurora cell-cycle literature (e.g. PMID 40195468 on Aurora A/B inhibition and non-mitotic division, PMID 31562563 on non-mitotic Aurora A functions, PMID 27396604 and PMID 32440158 on alisertib-induced cell cycle arrest/autophagy/apoptosis) but none defined the z>+20 frac_large_nucleus + nuc_area high-content signature we used, so we did not anchor the call on literature and should not claim we did.

Bottom line: the call was right because of repeated extreme morphology (e2,e3,e6,e7) + improving NSC majority (e4->e8) + cytoskeletal-intact visual exclusion (e5). The dose_response trends were correctly approved as saturated, not contradictory, and future runs should acquire the full dilution series with replicates at the low end to capture the true rising phase instead of inferring it.
